title: Rear Seatbelt Buckle Removal and Installation
introduction:
The rear buckle is secured to the floor beneath the seat cushion. This job starts with releasing the cushion’s locking tabs, then removing the buckle’s mounting bolt. I treat the buckle and belt tongue like a handshake: hearing the click is only the beginning—you still check that the connection holds and releases properly.

The instructions below cover cushion access, buckle removal, refitting and the buckle’s functional check. Retractor faults or warning-system concerns need the matching tests and repair references in Seatbelt Systems.

items.name: Prevent an unexpected start
items.detail: Park on level ground with the parking brake applied and wheels chocked; keep P selected on an automatic or a parked gear on a manual. Keep the engine stopped throughout. Disable remote start, if equipped, through Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup before dismantling anything. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the car, causing personal injury or death. If the setting needs ignition power, keep the valid intelligent access key inside. From confirmed OFF, press and release START/STOP without pressing either pedal to select engine-off ON. If already ON for the settings, leave it ON rather than toggling it. After the setting change, return ON to OFF by pressing and releasing the button without pressing a pedal; if already OFF, leave it OFF. Position both front seats fully forward for rear-cushion access before removing the key. With the ignition OFF, remove the key from the vehicle before service to prevent another person from starting the engine; an accidental start may cause serious personal injury. Review [Health and Safety Precautions](#/document/G1693189) before beginning.

items.name: Protect yourself around the seat and floor
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection during vehicle service. Wear protective gloves when handling parts with pointed or sharp edges. Failure to follow these precautions may result in serious personal injury.

items.name: Check the belt before replacing the buckle
items.detail: Before diagnosing or repairing the seatbelt system, examine the webbing for tears, fraying, cuts or stretching, and inspect the buckle and tongue assembly. These preliminary checks belong to [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856); changing the buckle does not establish that the rest of the belt is sound.

items.name: Fastener equipment
items.detail: Have a suitable tool for the buckle mounting bolt and a torque wrench capable of applying the installation torque given in the removal step. Move both front seats fully forward before releasing the rear cushion. Tool size is not specified. Keep everyone and all objects clear of the seat travel; never adjust the driver seat while the vehicle is moving. For manual seats, lift the bar beneath the front of the cushion, move the seat along its tracks, release the bar and rock the seat backward and forward to confirm it locks. For power seats, move the outboard seat-control switch forward or backward in the required travel direction. If ignition power is needed, use the valid key inside and the known OFF-to-engine-off-ON button sequence in preparation, without pressing either pedal; after positioning, return any ignition ON state to ignition OFF and remove the key before service. Do not toggle an ignition state already OFF.

items.name: Protect the cushion locking tabs
items.detail: The locking tabs are along the front edge of the rear cushion, at its floor attachments. Press them inward to release them before lifting the cushion. Pulling the cushion free without pressing the tabs can damage them. See [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168).

items.name: Buckle and tongue functional test
items.detail: Insert the tongue into the buckle: insertion must not require excessive effort, and the latch must click. Forcefully pull the webbing to check that the connection holds. Fully press the release button and allow the belt to release and retract; the button must operate without excessive effort, and the tongue must come out easily. Repeat the complete sequence 3 times. If the test reveals a concern, install a new buckle or retractor as required by the finding, using the matching removal and installation procedure. See [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856).

items.name: Keep a remaining fault on its diagnostic path
items.detail: If extraction, retraction, locking, warning-indicator or chime concerns remain, use the matching functional test or diagnostic referral in [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856). Its diagnostic work requires the Ford-specific practices in Diagnostic Methods. Those broader diagnostic procedures are separate from this buckle repair.

edits.text: NOTE: The RH buckle is shown; removal and installation of the LH buckle are similar.
edits.why: RH identifies the right-hand side and LH the left-hand side. Use the illustration to recognize the corresponding mounting point on the side being serviced.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The mounting-bolt torque appears with removal, but it governs tightening when the buckle goes back in.

edits.text:
Move both front seats fully forward. At the front edge of the rear seat cushion, press the locking tabs inward to release the cushion from the floor. Lift and release the cushion, then remove it.
Refer to: [Rear Seat Cushion](#/document/G1692168) (501-10B Rear Seats, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Moving the front seats creates working room. The cushion has locking attachments near either end of its front edge; release those attachments before lifting. The tabs are latches, not handles—hauling upward without releasing them can damage them.

edits.text:
Remove the mounting bolt, then remove the safety belt buckle.
During installation, tighten the bolt to 30 lb.ft (40 Nm).
edits.why: I use the drawing to distinguish the buckle mounting from nearby seat hardware: the blue buckle stalk ends in a floor-mounted bracket, and the arrow points to its magenta bolt. The torque applies when securing that bracket during refitting.

edits.text: NOTE: During installation, keep the safety belt webbing untwisted and leave the safety belts and buckles accessible to the occupants.
edits.why: Keep the belts and buckle heads clear as the cushion returns to position so they are not trapped underneath it. If a tongue is rotated or webbing remains twisted at a guide, stop and use the complete matching [Seatbelt Tongue Rotated On Belt](#/document/G1692226) or [Seatbelt Twisted at the Seatbelt Guide](#/document/G1726475) procedure, including any required trim access. Do not treat this buckle replacement as a partial substitute for those repairs or leave an unresolved twist.

edits.text: Install in reverse removal order: position the buckle at its floor mounting, install the bolt and tighten it to the torque specified in the removal step. Refit the rear seat cushion, keeping the belts and buckles accessible, and reengage its front locking tabs with the floor attachments. Return the front seats from their fully forward access positions.
edits.why: The buckle must be secured before the cushion covers its mounting. Reversing the access sequence also restores the cushion’s attachments while giving you a final opportunity to catch trapped or twisted webbing. To return the front seats, first clear all people and objects from their movement paths, then use the manual bar or outboard power switch described in preparation. Confirm a manual seat locks after release. If power requires ignition ON, keep the engine stopped and use the known-state button sequence only after all buckle and cushion work is complete. Finish with ignition OFF and the key outside, whether or not ignition power was used; keep the parked gear, parking brake and wheel restraints unchanged.

edits.text:
Check the active restraint system for correct operation. Carry out the buckle-and-tongue functional test described in the completion checks, and use the appropriate additional tests if another seatbelt concern remains.
Refer to: [Seatbelt Systems](#/document/G1883856) (501-20A Seatbelt Systems, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The functional check establishes whether the tongue enters freely, latches, stays retained under a forceful pull and releases freely. A remaining concern requires the indicated new buckle or retractor and its matching repair procedure. Warning or chime faults belong on the linked diagnostic path; a fresh buckle is not a diagnosis.

editorialRevision.scope: Stationary known-state preparation; owner-backed manual/power front-seat access and restoration with final ignition OFF; optional partial twist repairs replaced with complete matching procedure referrals and stop-unresolved instruction. Primary action text, torque and buckle functional test unchanged. Full original technical review retained; bounded increment review separate.
